snippet.description:
Tom Felton, who played Draco Malfoy in the Harry Potter movies, shares a story about his worst day on set, which involved Alan Rickman, who played the iconic character of Professor Snape. Felton recounts a moment when he accidentally stepped on Rickman's cloak, causing the scene to come to a halt. Rickman then scolded Felton for his mistake, leaving him feeling embarrassed and ashamed.

A fart machine was hidden inside his sleeping bag, and Gambon kept secretly pressing it mid-take.

**DESCRIPTION**

He played the coldest, most feared professor at Hogwarts. But off camera, Alan Rickman was doing something that will make you tear up. 🥹

According to Gary Oldman, Rickman quietly welcomed children from schools and hospitals onto the Harry Potter sets. There were no cameras and no headlines. He walked them around, showed them the magic up close, and let kids facing some of the hardest days of their lives step inside the world they loved most.

Think about that for a second. The actor behind Professor Snape, the character who made a whole generation nervous, was the same man helping children feel like they truly belonged at Hogwarts.

Ten years after his passing, this memory still hits differently. It's proof that the actors who play the toughest characters on screen are often the kindest people in real life. And the real magic was never in the wand. It was in showing up for someone who needed a little wonder.

Alan Rickman gave those kids something no movie ticket ever could: a moment where the story became real. ✨
